items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.summary: The article shows generalist AI models outperform specialist policies in robot manipulation tasks, analyzing agentic manipulation policies (AMPs).
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it suggests broader, more reliable AI control for robotics.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.summary: The paper proposes CPU-ARC, a method that caches reasoning steps so LLMs can reuse solutions for new tasks, reducing redundant computation.
items.whyItMatters: It could speed up on‑CPU inference and lower costs for developers using large language models.

items.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
items.summary: The paper shows ReLU networks with limited neurons form a weakly closed set in Sobolev space, ensuring energy minimizers exist for methods like Deep Ritz.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it guarantees convergence and optimality for popular neural network training techniques.

items.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
items.summary: FlowMoP introduces a stochastic multi-person motion prediction model using conditional flow matching to generate diverse future trajectories for each agent.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more realistic, uncertainty-aware planning for autonomous systems interacting with humans.

items.title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
items.summary: The paper shows how graded convolutional networks achieve scale invariance and blur robustness by using scale‑normalized jets and weighted spheres.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it offers a principled way to build neural nets that handle size changes and blur without extra training.

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper examines how reliable majority-vote pseudo-labels are for test-time reinforcement learning of language models, breaking down errors into bias and rollout variation.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding pseudo-label trustworthiness helps improve adaptive language model performance on new data.

items.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
items.summary: CodeQuant2 improves low‑precision large reasoning models by mitigating outliers and adapting clustering during early decoding steps.
items.whyItMatters: It reduces inference cost while preserving reasoning accuracy for tech‑savvy users.

items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.summary: GRAC uses graph-based retrieval to generate automated captions for surgical scenes, aiming to streamline operative report creation.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it automates documentation, saving time and improving surgical training.

items.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: The paper presents Grasp-TAGS, a method that uses critic distillation to select task-aware grasps for mobile manipulators performing long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It improves reliability of mobile robots handling large objects, benefiting warehouse automation and service robotics.

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.summary: The paper proposes a flow-guided method that aligns source modalities into a target space, preserving global structure and instance-level correspondence for downstream tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers benefit from improved multimodal integration and accurate downstream analysis.

items.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
items.summary: The article investigates whether a sender that only transmits hash bits, with a language model at the receiver, can send short English texts more cheaply than a fully trained sender, using a pre‑registered experiment on 1,000 Taskmaster‑1 utterances.
items.whyItMatters: It explores a novel, potentially lower‑cost communication protocol that could reduce bandwidth and computation for edge devices.

items.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.summary: The article argues embodied AI will shift to general-purpose models, using software to render physical environments and provide controls for agents.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should watch this trend for its impact on AI flexibility and cross-domain applications.

items.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
items.summary: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. items.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
items.summary: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". The dataset PigAirwayPressure is not an outlier. Although the archive is…

items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.summary: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality…

items.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during…

items.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
items.summary: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented…

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms…

items.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
items.summary: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein…

items.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the…
